sections.title: Incoming Quality Certificates
sections.text:
11.1 Incoming Quality Certificates
The first step toward integrating quality certificates into the procurement process
begins when the person overseeing QM operations assigns a certificate type, which is
needed for a procured material. A certificate type confirms the specific type of certifi-
cate that the company needs from the supplier at the time of goods receipt and shows
compliance with the quality standards set by the company. The next step is to put the
necessary control levels in place for incoming quality certificate submission. Such con-
trol levels can vary from a lenient information message to a more stringent error mes-
sage that occurs if the incoming certificate doesn’t accompany the receipt of the goods.

11 Quality Certificates
502
An information message by the system simply informs the warehouse staff of the
missing quality certificate. An error message doesn’t allow for a goods receipt until the
supplier submits the quality certificate.
Let’s get started with setting up the configuration basics.

sections.title: Configuring the Control Key
sections.text:
11.1.1 Configuring the Control Key
A control key controls the allowed (or disallowed) business functions by setting the
parameters or settings that the system should check during transaction processing. To
define a new control key or make changes to an existing one, follow menu path SAP
IMG  Quality Management  QM in Logistics  QM in Procurement  Define Control Keys.
In the screen that appears, select QM Control Key 0005 followed by choosing Details
and Figure 11.1 will appear.
Figure 11.1 Control Key for QM in Procurement
Select at least the two checkboxes for Release Required and Certificate Required. The
Release Required checkbox confirms that the user must maintain the supplier’s rela-
tionship to the material before initiating any procurement activity in the system. This
relationship is referred to as a quality information record, which we’ll discuss in Section
11.1.3. The Certificate Required checkbox ensures that the supplier submits an incoming
© 

503
11.1 Incoming Quality Certificates
quality certificate at the time of goods delivery. Although these are related to QM, the
remaining checkboxes aren’t directly related to incoming quality certificates.
Tips and Tricks
You can define a new control key if the standard control keys available in SAP S/4HANA
don’t fulfill your business requirements.

sections.title: Define Control Functions for Certificate Processing
sections.text:
11.1.2 Define Control Functions for Certificate Processing
Just like a control key, you also assign a certificate type in the material master data and
assign further control functions for incoming quality certificates. To define the control
function of a specific certificate type, use Transaction V_TQ05 or follow menu path SAP
IMG  Quality Management  QM in Logistics  QM in Procurement  Define Keys for Cer-
tificate Processing. Choose Define Certificate Types.
The screen that appears contains a list of the standard available certificate types. You
can either use the available certificate types or define a new one. If the existing certifi-
cate types meet your company’s business needs, then we suggest that you use them as
is or make changes to them. For this example, we create a new Certificate Type, 0008,
as shown in Figure 11.2.
Figure 11.2 Detailed Screen of Certificate Type 0008
To gain a better understanding of each option in Figure 11.2, refer to Table 11.1.

11 Quality Certificates
504
The configuration for incoming certificates is now complete. The next step is to main-
tain the relevant information in the material master data and create the quality infor-
mation record.

sections.title: Master Data for Incoming Quality Certificates
sections.text:
11.1.3 Master Data for Incoming Quality Certificates
You need to set up the QM master data for the incoming quality certificate in SAP
S/4HANA before starting the procurement process. We’ll discuss the required master
data in the following sections.
Certificate Type Control Detail of Control Function
Certificate for Each PO Item The system requires a separate certificate for each item in the
purchase order. If not selected, then one certificate is suffi-
cient for the entire purchase order containing multiple line
items.
Certificate for Each GR Item The system requires a separate certificate for each item on the
goods receipt. If not selected, then one certificate is sufficient
for the entire goods receipt containing multiple line items.
Certificate Check Required This checkbox is generally used in business scenarios involv-
ing electronic certificates and in which the user must still
check the certificate to ensure that all parameters of the
ordered goods are in conformity.
Control Without Certificate Enforces a required action if a certificate isn’t received. The
various available options include no information message,
just an information message, warning message, error mes-
sage, moving material, and blocked stock.
Enhanced Certificate Pro-
cessing
Used for enhanced certificate processing.
No Certificate Confirmation
at GR
With selection of this checkbox, as well as the Enhanced
Certifcate Processing checkbox, the business user must
separately record the incoming certificate instead of simply
confirming certificate receipt at the time of material goods
receipt.
Rem. Deadline (Days) This option is maintained in number of days to create a
system-generated reminder if the supplier fails to deliver
the quality certificate after the delivery of goods.
Escalation Deadline Also maintained in number of days, this option stipulates that
the system must escalate the reminder if the supplier still fails
to deliver or submit the quality certificate.
Table 11.1 Certificate Type Options
© 

505
11.1 Incoming Quality Certificates
Certificate Details in the QM View in the Material Master
Figure 11.3 shows the Quality Management view of the material master that was
accessed by using Transaction MM02 and entering material RM129 and plant 1710. In
the ensuing popup to select material views, choose the Quality Management view and
press (Enter). Select the QM in Procur. Active checkbox if you need a quality informa-
tion record (otherwise known as a relationship between the supplier and the material)
to exist while creating a purchase order. Because this is a procurement process, we rec-
ommend that you select this checkbox. Assign QM Control Key 0005 and Certificate
Type 0008. These are the same two configuration objects (the QM control key and the
certificate type) that you managed in the previous section.
Figure 11.3 Assigning QM Control Key and Certificate Type in the Material Master Quality
Management View
Note
Although the focus of this chapter is on quality certificates, make sure that other QM
master data elements for this material (RM129)—such as the relevant inspection type
activation in the material master, master inspection characteristics, inspection, and
plan—are already available in the system.
Quality Information Record
Because you selected the QM in Procur. Active checkbox, as shown in Figure 11.3, you
need to define a relationship between a material and the supplier as a part of the QM
master data. To create a quality information record, use Transaction QI01 or follow
menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Logistics Master Data 
Quality Info Record: Procurement  Create. On the initial screen that appears for the cre-
ation of a quality information record, enter Material “RM129”, Supplier “17300006”,
and Plant “1710”, and then press (Enter) so that the screen in Figure 11.4 appears.
On this screen, choose the Inspection Control tab, and then choose Inspection Active If
Supplier Not Certified in Insp. Control. This ensures that in the case of an uncertified
supplier, the system checks that there is an incoming certificate for the relevant

11 Quality Certificates
506
material (RM129) procured from the supplier (17300006). Other option is here regard-
less of the fact that a supplier is certified; otherwise, it will still have to go through the
quality inspection and quality control process. Finally, it also has an option that a sup-
plier is exempted from quality certification process for this specific material. Save the
quality information record.
This step completes the important QM master data you need to implement incoming
certificates in procurement processes. However, to fully understand the completeness
and implications of configuration and master data in procurement processes, we’ll run
an end-to-end procurement cycle of creating a purchase order, posting the goods
receipt of the same purchase order, and managing missing information in incoming
certificates in the next sections. We’ll also explain how to enter incoming certificate
details with reference to the purchase order and its line-item number, as well as gener-
ate reminders to suppliers to submit missing certificates against the goods supplied.
Figure 11.4 Quality Information Record

sections.title: Create a Purchase Order
sections.text:
11.1.4 Create a Purchase Order
To create the purchase order, use Transaction ME21N or follow menu path Logistics 
Materials Management  Purchasing  Purchase Order  Create  Supplier/Supplying
Plant Known. In the screen that appears, enter Supplier “17300006”, material “RM129”,
a quantity of 100 EA, and Plant “1710” and can be seen when the Item Overview tab
located in the center of the screen is expanded (see Figure 11.5).
Notice that QA Control Key 0005 is activated in the Delivery tab, and a certificate is
required at the time of goods receipt (delivery) of the material against the purchase

507
11.1 Incoming Quality Certificates
order’s line-item number. Further, the associated CertificateType is 0008 as shown
here. Save the purchase order, and the system generates purchase order number
4500001824.
Figure 11.5 Item Detail of Purchase Order for Procured Material

sections.title: Goods Receipt against the Purchase Order
sections.text:
11.1.5 Goods Receipt against the Purchase Order
Now, you’ll record goods receipt for purchase order number 4500001824. Use Transac-
tion MIGO or follow menu path Logistics  Materials Management  Inventory Manage-
ment  Goods Movement  Goods Movement. In the screen that appears, enter the
purchase order number previously created (“4500001824”), and press (Enter) (see
Figure 11.6).
Figure 11.6 Warning Message for Missing Incoming Certificate on Goods Receipt

11 Quality Certificates
508
To ensure that all information is complete on the goods receipt screen, choose Check
(not shown, but located on the bottom-right side of the screen). A popup appears to
inform you that a certificate of type 0008 (inspection certificate) is required. You can
now confirm this warning by pressing (Enter) again to save the document. If this error
message appeared on the screen in Figure 11.2, the system wouldn’t be allowed to pro-
ceed until the incoming certificate was entered in the system.

sections.title: Incoming Inspection Certificate
sections.text:
11.1.6 Incoming Inspection Certificate
To bring greater visibility into and improved tracking of incoming quality certificates,
there are a few statuses that the warehouse supervisor can use to reflect whether the
certificate is in-process or if it has been received. Some of these statuses are Certificate
Is Expected, Certificate Filed and Inspected, and Certificate Is Defective. There are two
additional system statuses—either a reminder or a more urgent, Escalated warning—
that the system automatically sends to a supplier who hasn’t yet sent a quality certifi-
cate.
Create an incoming inspection certificate by using Transaction QC51 or menu path
Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Certificates  Incoming  Create. In the screen
that appears, enter the purchase order number, followed by the item number of the
purchase order, and press (Enter). You’ll see a popup, as shown in Figure 11.7, to inform
you that this specific purchase order has a pending incoming certificate. Choose line
item 201 (the incoming quality certificate number), and then choose Continue (not
shown). The screen in Figure 11.8 appears.
Figure 11.7 Missing Incoming Certificate Information
Here, and just for the purpose of this example, we define that the certificate is expected
against the entered purchase order (see Figure 11.8).
In other words, we haven’t updated the status of this certificate. With this certificate
status, you can send a reminder to the supplier to expedite certificate submission.
Notice that there are several other statuses of an incoming certificate that the business
user can manually update, and these should be based on the actual status of the certif-
icate. The system automatically updates the status when the user performs certain
© 

509
11.1 Incoming Quality Certificates
functions, such as sending a reminder to a supplier or escalating nonreceipt of a certif-
icate. Save your entries.
Figure 11.8 Certificate Data for Incoming Quality Certificate

sections.title: Incoming Certificate Worklist
sections.text:
11.1.7 Incoming Certificate Worklist
There are instances when the company agrees with the supplier to submit the incom-
ing quality certificate within an agreed-upon grace period, for example, within three
days after goods delivery. This may be the case when results of a few chemical tests take
longer to become available, and the supplier takes correspondingly more time to sub-
mit the requisite quality certificate. If the supplier fails to submit the quality certificate
within the agreed-upon grace period, the system sends a reminder message to the sup-
plier about the missing quality certificate.
To track the expected or missing incoming certificates you need to follow up on with
suppliers, the system provides the intuitive capability to send reminders in the form of
emails, as Adobe Acrobat documents, or simply by mail.
To access an incoming inspection certificate’s QM worklist, use Transaction QC55 or fol-
low menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Certificates  Incoming  Work-
list. Figure 11.9 shows the initial screen in which you enter the relevant parameters so
that the system creates a worklist for further action. For this example, provide a specific

11 Quality Certificates
510
Certificate (201), and enter “1” for the status certificate receipt (Status Cert. Receipt),
located on the upper half of the screen (not shown here). This status of the expected
certificates enables you to send reminders to suppliers. SAP provides preconfigured
output formats, such as QM_CERT_REMIND, which you can customize using ABAP
resources to meet your company’s specific business needs.
Choose Execute (not shown), and the system displays the screen shown in Figure 11.10,
which is the QM worklist for an incoming certificate in procurement. Choose the rele-
vant items, and then choose Dunning Notices to enable the system to create reminders.
Figure 11.9 QM Worklist: Quality Certificates in Procurement
Figure 11.10 QM Worklist for Quality Certificates in Procurement
© 

511
11.1 Incoming Quality Certificates
You’ll see a message that appears if the deadline to submit the certificate hasn’t yet
been exceeded. You can still confirm the message and create the reminder by clicking
the Yes button.
Figure 11.11 shows the print preview of the incoming certificate receipt reminder. To
bring up the print preview of the incoming certificate, select the line item from the
worklist, and choose Print Preview. The incoming certificate contains all the relevant
details needed to ensure that the supplier sends or submits the needed certificate as
soon as possible. Notice that it contains certificate type 0008, which you had previ-
ously configured.
Figure 11.11 Print Preview of Certificate Receipt Reminder
Once the system sends the reminder, it automatically updates the status of the certifi-
cate to 3, which denotes that the reminder for the certificate is sent (refer to Figure 11.8).
If the supplier still fails to submit the quality certificate after receiving a certificate sub-
mission reminder, then the next logical step is to escalate it to reflect the urgency of
certificate submission. The urgency exists because the warehouse supervisor is unable
to issue the supplier-delivered material to production or maintenance processes,
thereby disrupting the logistics, maintenance, or supply chain functions of the com-
pany. As in the case of the incoming certificate reminder message, the system sends an
escalation message to the defaulting supplier.
The steps involved in sending escalation notices to a supplier are the same as those for
sending reminders. On the initial parameters selection screen (Transaction QC55), set
the Status of the certificate to “3” to denote that the supplier was previously sent the
reminder; this time, the system triggers an escalation note during the dunning process.

11 Quality Certificates
512
Note
You can also transfer the data of the incoming quality certificate into the inspection lot
by using an intermediary document (IDoc). IDocs are beyond the scope of this book.

sections.title: Outgoing Quality Certificates
sections.text:
11.2 Outgoing Quality Certificates
Be it a business need or a practice to send accompanying outgoing quality certificates
for every delivery of the customer’s order to enable sharing quality results for inter-
company communication, it’s quick and easy to integrate outgoing quality certificates
in QM. Most of the needed groundwork can be successfully undertaken by an SAP func-
tional consultant or even by the client’s business users who have sufficient exposure to
the SAP S/4HANA system. Outgoing quality certificates integrate with SAP S/4HANA
Sales, where goods delivered to the customer are accompanied by the relevant (outgo-
ing) quality certificate.
A practical approach is to thoroughly assess and evaluate all the areas and processes in
which different and diverse usages of outgoing quality certificates are needed and can
be implemented. Upon completing this activity and gaining insight into the series of
activities involved, you may treat implementing an outgoing quality certificate as a
mini project or part of an ongoing business processes improvement.
In the sales process, the company needs to engage the person looking after the QM
operations to define the certificate type that will accompany its product as a physical
document at the time of goods dispatch to the customer. The next step is to define a
certificate profile in the system, consisting of the inspection results of the physical and
chemical attributes of the product. The quality inspector conducts a quality inspection
on the product, consisting of various tests, and eventually records the actual results in
the system. The quality inspector prints these actual inspection results on the outgoing
quality certificate. This printed outgoing quality certificate is the actual physical docu-
ment that the company sends to its customer with each goods dispatch.
Let’s now begin with the configuration steps involved in setting up outgoing quality
certificates.

sections.title: Define Keys for Certificate Processing
sections.text:
11.2.1 Define Keys for Certificate Processing
You have to assign a certificate type when you define a certificate profile for the out-
going certificate. You can either use the standard certificate keys available in the SAP
S/4HANA system or create a new key.
To create a new control key for a certificate type, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality
Management  Quality Certificates  Certificate Profile  Define Keys for Certificate Pro-
cessing. In the popup that opens, double-click Define Certificate Types. The ensuing
© 

513
11.2 Outgoing Quality Certificates
screen contains a standard list of available certificate types. As already mentioned, here
you can either use an available certificate type or create a new one. In this example, use
standard certificate type E23C, which is already available in the SAP S/4HANA system.
This is the only configuration step you need for the outgoing quality certificate pro-
cess. The next step is to create or update the QM master data that is specific to outgoing
quality certificates.

sections.title: Master Data for Outgoing Quality Certificates
sections.text:
11.2.2 Master Data for Outgoing Quality Certificates
We begin with QM master data you need to set up for outgoing quality certificates in
the SAP S/4HANA system. The required QM master data is the certificate profile and the
assignment of the certificate profile, which we’ll discuss in the following sections.
Note
Make sure that other QM master data elements for the material, such as the relevant
inspection type activation in the material master, master inspection characteristics,
and inspection plan, are already created and available in the system.
Certificate Profile
The first step in generating an outgoing quality certificate is to create a certificate pro-
file. A certificate profile holds extensive user-defined information about what the com-
pany would like to see in the printout of its outgoing quality certificate and how it
should be presented. For example, the company may have five different master inspec-
tion characteristics for results recording of a material but wants only two master
inspection characteristics printed on the outgoing quality certificate. Similarly, you
can group together several materials with the same set of master inspection character-
istics in one certificate profile, thereby reducing the time and effort you put into main-
taining the QM master data.
To create a new certificate profile, use Transaction QC01 or follow menu path Logistics 
Quality Management  Quality Certificates  Outgoing  Certificate Profile  Create. The
initial screen of certificate profile creation appears; for this example, enter
“QMCERT01” for the certificate profile Name, and the certificate type given is E23C (not
shown). Notice that this is the same certificate type that we just covered in Section 11.2.1.
Choose Header Data, enter a short description of the certificate profile (not shown), and
the screen in Figure 11.12 appears. Assign an SAPscript form that the system will use as
an output layout. For this example, we use the standard SAPscript that SAP delivers,
which is QM_QCERT_01. You can engage an ABAP resource to configure and make
available a company-specific printout (or output) of the certificate. For example, the
outgoing quality certificate’s script may contain the company’s logo, as well as the offi-
cial address and specific text that the company would like to appear on the certificate.

11 Quality Certificates
514
Figure 11.12 Certificate Profile
Select the Accepted Lots Only checkbox, which means that the system allows printout
of only outgoing quality certificates for which the usage decision is recorded as
accepted. This ensures that inspection lots with rejected usage decisions are neither
inadvertently printed nor circulated.
You can also restrict the inspection type for which the certificate profile becomes avail-
able, but this isn’t necessary or mandatory. It just provides additional control function-
ality. For this example, we restrict the certificate profile Inspection Lot Origin to 89 only
(not shown but located further down the same screen).
Choose the Materials button to see the screen in Figure 11.13, where you assign the
material (or materials) with its respective inspection origin and inspection types, which
use certificate profile QMCERT01.
Notice the Accptd checkbox, used to ensure that the system uses only accepted inspec-
tion lots of materials with accepted usage decisions. In addition, notice that in the very
last column, Min QScore, you can even control the minimum quality score an inspec-
tion lot must have (after its usage decision) for the system to allow creation of an outgo-
ing quality certificate. This is another control criterion that companies often use in their
outgoing quality certificate processing. Here, you can enter several materials with the
same master inspection characteristics and different inspection types, thus saving time
and effort in the master data maintenance required for outgoing quality certificates.
© 

515
11.2 Outgoing Quality Certificates
Figure 11.13 Material Assignment to Certificate Profile
For this example, assign Material “QM001” with its inspection Origin and Insp. Type as
“89”, and select the Accptd checkbox. Choose Continue, which takes you back to the
screen in Figure 11.12. Choose Characteristics, and this leads to the screen in Figure 11.14,
which shows the characteristic overview of the certificate profile. Here, you assign all
the master inspection characteristics required on printout/output of an outgoing qual-
ity certificate. Enter previously created master inspection characteristics “QMHT10”,
“PURITY”, and “VISINSP”, and make additional selections with respect to these master
inspection characteristics.
Here, you have complete control over how you would like the output of an outgoing
quality certificate to look. Further, you also have the option to output the actual value
of the results or its upper or lower ranges, or even average results. Scroll to the right
side of the screen in Figure 11.14, and the screen in Figure 11.15 appears. Here, the system
offers further controls and options for the certificate’s output, including decimal
places, actual value or average value of the master inspection characteristic, and
whether the master inspection characteristic description needs to be different (in the
certificate’s output) than what’s maintained in the SAP S/4HANA system.

11 Quality Certificates
516
Figure 11.14 Characteristics Data of Certificate Profile
After entering master inspection characteristics with the requisite details, choose Back
and then Release Profile, and save the certificate profile. A released certificate profile
can always be locked if there is any such business need. Choose the lock to achieve this.
If the certificate profile is already released, then the icon changes to Block Profile, as
shown earlier in Figure 11.12.
Figure 11.15 Certification Profile
Certificate Profile Assignment
After certificate profile creation, you need to assign it to either a material or group of
materials or to a material-customer combination. To create a new assignment for the
certificate profile, use Transaction QC15 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality
Management  Quality Certificates  Outgoing  Certificate Profile  Assignment  Create.
Figure 11.16 shows the initial screen for the assignment of the certificate profile. The
Assignment type QCA1 is standard; once you enter it, choose Key from the Edit menu
© 

517
11.2 Outgoing Quality Certificates
bar located on the top of the screen (or simply press (Enter)) to select the key combina-
tion. For this example, choose Material, and press (Enter), which leads to the screen in
Figure 11.17.
Figure 11.16 Assignment of Certificate Profile
Figure 11.17 Assignment of Materials to Certificate Profile
In Figure 11.17, select the same material, QM001; the certificate profile, QMCERT01; the
certificate type, E23C; and the certificate profile version, which is 1.

sections.title: Business Processes in Outgoing Quality Certificates
sections.text:
11.2.3 Business Processes in Outgoing Quality Certificates
To explain the actual use of all the QM master data created so far and how to finally cre-
ate the outgoing quality certificate, let’s now cover the business process flow in this
section. This end-to-end business process flow consists of four steps:
1. Creating a manual inspection lot
2. Results recording
3. Usage decision
4. Creating the outgoing quality certificate

11 Quality Certificates
518
We’ll create a manual inspection lot for which we first perform results recording, fol-
lowed by making a usage decision. The business process concludes with actual creation
and output of the outgoing quality certificate.
Note
Although this example focuses on creating a manual inspection lot of inspection type
89 and subsequent business processes to generate the outgoing quality certificate, the
same logic and fundamentals for generating the outgoing quality certificate apply if
your company uses inspection data from other inspection types and recorded results.
These other inspection types may be, for example, inspection type 04 for finished
goods inspection or inspection type 10 for inspection at the time of goods issuance
against a sales order. You just need to make the relevant settings in the master data
that we covered in the prior section.
Create Inspection Lot
To create a manual inspection lot, use Transaction QA01 or menu path Logistics  Qual-
ity Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot  Processing  Create. On the initial
screen in this case, enter Material “QM001”, Plant “1710”, and Inspection Type “89”, and
press (Enter). This leads to the screen in Figure 11.18, which shows the detailed screen
for manual inspection lot creation, in which Insp. Lot Quantity is the mandatory field.
Figure 11.18 Inspection Lot Creation
© 

519
11.2 Outgoing Quality Certificates
Notice that at the time of manual inspection lot creation, the system generates an
inspection lot number. In this example, this inspection lot number is 890000000302.
Enter an inspection lot quantity of “10”. This inspection lot number and batch number
(if a material is batch-managed) will remain your reference throughout the remaining
business process steps leading to the outgoing quality certificate. Save the entries.
Results Recording
Record results of the just created inspection lot. To do so, use Transaction QE01, enter
inspection lot “890000000302” on the initial screen, and press (Enter). In the results
recording screen, enter the results of the three master inspection characteristics that
are within the acceptable range. Because the results of the three master inspection
characteristics are within the Specifications, the system automatically valuates them as
Accepted, with the corresponding green checkmark (see Figure 11.19).
Figure 11.19 Usage Decision
Usage Decision
With results recording for the inspection lot entered in the system, the next step is the
usage decision. For the usage decision, use Transaction QA11 and, on the initial screen,
enter inspection lot “890000000302”. Press (Enter) to see the screen in Figure 11.19,
where you record the usage decision for the inspection lot by entering “A” for the UD
Code for acceptance of the inspection lot. Save your entries.

11 Quality Certificates
520
Outgoing Quality Certificate Creation
You can create an outgoing quality certificate with reference to a delivery, batch num-
ber, or inspection lot. For this example, create the certificate with reference to inspec-
tion lot 890000000302. Use Transaction QC21 or menu path Logistics  Quality
Management  Quality Certificates  Outgoing  Certificate Creation  For Inspection Lot.
Figure 11.20 shows the initial screen to enter the relevant parameters. Enter inspection
lot “890000000301” for which you just entered the results and the usage decision.
Alternately, for a batch-managed material, use Transaction QC22, and enter the mate-
rial (“QM001”) together with its corresponding batch (“500”), as shown in Figure 11.20.
Select Choose Recipient to select whether the certificate’s recipient is a customer num-
ber, customer contact person, supplier number, user-definable address, or simply no
recipient. For this example, choose User-Definable Address and then choose Continue.
Next, manually enter the address of the person to whom you want to send the outgo-
ing quality certificate.
Figure 11.20 Outgoing Quality Certificate Creation
Choose Execute (not shown but located on the lower right of the screen), and this leads
to the print output option, in which you enter the local printer “LP01” and then choose
Print Preview, which leads to the print preview of the outgoing quality certificate with
all the relevant details (see Figure 11.21). The certificate contains the manually typed
address (user-definable address), the material number, its description, the inspection
lot number, the batch number, the recorded results of the master inspection character-
istics, and the upper and lower limits. A partial print preview of the outgoing quality
certificate is shown in Figure 11.21.
© 

521

sections.title: Summary
sections.text:
11.3 Summary
Figure 11.21 Print Preview of Outgoing Quality Certificate
Note
Available in the same outgoing quality certificate menu path of QM, you’ll also find
separate transactions for delivery (Transaction QC20), batch (Transaction QC22), and
multiple specifications (Transaction QCMS).
11.3 Summary
Quality certificates help validate that a product conforms to predefined specifications.
SAP offers two types of quality certificates: incoming quality certificates and outgoing
quality certificates. An incoming quality certificate is used to compare and measure
incoming goods with a company’s quality specifications to make sure they meet those
standards.
Outgoing quality certificates perform a similar function for products leaving the com-
pany’s premises. Used in conjunction with the sales and delivery process, an outgoing
quality certificate is a document which confirms that the delivered good conforms to
the customer’s specifications. The certificate is delivered at the time the goods are
delivered to the customer.
The next chapter covers the quality notification and quality issue management pro-
cesses.

©
